name: חֶצְרוֹן
summary: Two men who went down into Egypt with Jacob: Hezron son of Reuben, head of the Hezronite clan of Reuben, and Hezron son of Perez, grandson of Judah, father of Ram and so an ancestor of David and of Jesus (Rut 4:18–22; Mat 1:3). The name is חָצֵר with the ending ־וֹן, as of a place or a quality: “of the enclosure” or “of the settlement”, but scripture does not explain it. A town on Judah’s southern border has the same name (Jos 15:3).

evidence.note: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, חֶצְרוֹן and Carmi.
The sons of Perez: חֶצְרוֹן and Hamul.
Of Hezron, the clan of הַחֶצְרוֹנִי, the Hezronite, in Reuben.
Perez fathered Hezron, Hezron fathered Ram: the line to David.
Φάρες δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑσρώμ: Hezron in the genealogy of Jesus.
The root’s noun: חֲצֵרִים, unwalled settlements.
The root’s noun: חָצֵר, an enclosed court.

note: BDB key h.fb.am also counts the town Hezron (Jos 15:3) and Kerioth-hezron (Jos 15:25), which are places; h.fb.an is the gentilic חֶצְרוֹנִי (Num 26:6, 21). TIPNR also files Jos 15:25’s Hezron under Hazor@Jos.11.1 (a place). Which of the root’s two older roots (enclosure, ṯ̣; settlement, ṣ́) the name is formed from cannot be told from Hebrew spelling; no cognate name has been found.
